          Coastguard plane involved in major rescue after sailing vessel capsizes

          A sailor was rescued

          Comments0
          News
          Abigail Neep
          09:38, 03 Nov 2026
          Listen to audio version of this article
          Sponsored by
          0:00 / 1:18
          Instaread

          A sailor has been rescued after his vessel capsized 190 nautical miles off the coast.

          ‌
          ‌

          A distress report was made at around 1.55pm on Monday, November 2, after the solo sailor’s vessel capsized southwest of Mizen Head in Ireland.

          ‌

          CornwallLive understands a fixed-wing aircraft from Cornwall Airport Newquay was deployed to help with the rescue operation.

          ‌

          Eight vehicles catch fire in Cornwall village

          Don't let an algorithm decide what Cornwall news you see - click here to add CornwallLive as your preferred Google source.

          The man was located by an HM Coastguard aeroplane with his vessel and later recovered safe and well aboard a cargo vessel that had responded to a broadcast request for assistance.

          ‌

          A spokesperson for HM Coastguard said: “A solo sailor whose sailing vessel was reported to have capsized about 190 nautical miles south-west of Mizen Head, Ireland, was rescued in an operation coordinated by HM Coastguard.

          “The distress report was made at about 1.55pm on 2 November. The sailing vessel's registered Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon (EPRIB) was also activated.

          Article continues below

          “The man was located with his vessel by an HM Coastguard aeroplane and later recovered safe and well onto a cargo vessel, which had responded to a broadcast request to assist, for transfer to Ireland.”
